assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I heard the school might make every student do community service. I don't think you should make it a rule. Service is good and you can still tell kids to do it, but forcing us is a bad idea.

My first reason is that helping people only works if you want to be there. My friend Dana tutors second graders in reading two times a week. She knows which kids are stuck on which sounds. One boy will only read about sharks so she brings him shark books every time. Now think about a kid who got sent there because he has to. He would be looking at the clock the whole time and little kids can tell when you don't care about them. So the second grader gets a bad tutor and the older kid just learns that helping people is one more boring thing to get done.

My second reason is time. Not everybody has the same amount. Some kids in my class have nothing to do after school. But other kids have to go home and watch there little brothers and sisters until their mom or dad gets off work. Some of the older kids I know work at the grocery store until nine at night. They are already helping somebody and their family needs them. If you make everyone do forty hours it is way harder for them then for a kid with free afternoons. That isn't fair at all.

Also I worry about the places we would get sent to. The food pantry by my house only has two people working there. If sixty kids showed up and all of us needed a signature, those two people would spend the whole day making up jobs for us and signing papers. They wouldn't get to do there real work. My friends pick up litter on Saturdays and it works because only about ten people come and they all want to be there.

I think there is a better way to do this. You could make service a class we can pick, or let clubs do projects during school. You could give awards to kids who do a lot of hours. You should also count the stuff kids already do for their families, because that is helping too.

Thank you for listening to what a student thinks.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the plan to make every student do community service. I do not think it should be required. The school can still tell us about it and post the sign up sheets.

My first reason is that service only works when the person wants to be there. A girl in my class named Dana tutors second graders in reading two times a week. She knows which kids are stuck on which sounds. She brings shark books for one boy because sharks are the only thing he will read about. Now think about a student who got sent there and just stares at the clock. A seven year old can tell. The kid gets a really bad tutor, and the student starts to think of it as one more chore, the same as detention.

My second reason is time. Some kids in my class have nothing to do after school. Others stock shelves at a grocery store until nine, or they go home and watch their little brothers and sisters until a parent gets off work. Those students are already serving somebody. They come to school so tired. Forty hours would be very hard for them, and it is not fair to make it cost them more than everybody else. Some of them would have to pick between a paycheck and a diploma. A school should never force that on a kid.

The third problem is the places we would get sent to. The food pantry by my house only has two workers who get paid. If sixty teenagers show up needing signatures, those two people will lose the whole afternoon making up jobs and filling out forms. That does not feed anybody who is hungry. The litter crews on my street work because ten people show up on Saturday with gloves and bags, and nobody had to drag them there.

There is another way to do this. You could make service a class that counts toward graduation. Clubs could do projects during the school day. Students who put in a lot of hours could get their names read at the ceremony. You could also count the work kids already do for their families. Then nobody gets punished because they do not have the time.

Thank you for reading a student's view before you decide.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
